target.title: ProxyFix: use the original client address
target.description: Behind several proxies, X-Forwarded-For lists every hop. Use the first entry, which is the original client, instead of counting from the right. Also simplifies the host:port split for X-Forwarded-Host.

summary: ProxyFix now takes the first entry from X-Forwarded-For instead of counting from the right, and simplifies IPv6 host-port splitting for X-Forwarded-Host.

suspects.title: IPv6 host parsing without brackets breaks rsplit on colon
suspects.problem: Removing the check for `endswith("]")` means an IPv6 address without a port containing colons (e.g. `2001:db8::1`) will have its last component incorrectly split as a port using `rsplit(":", 1)`.
suspects.how_to_check: Check tests or how `x_host` is validated or handled across the codebase, and verify if IPv6 addresses without ports can be passed in `X-Forwarded-Host`.

suspects.title: Ignoring the trusted count for X-Forwarded-For
suspects.problem: The code now unconditionally takes `values[0]` as the original client address whenever `len(values) >= trusted`, completely ignoring the `trusted` parameter value which determines how many proxies are trusted to append correct headers.
suspects.how_to_check: Inspect tests for ProxyFix to see how `x_for` and `trusted` values interact and whether returning index 0 is expected for untrusted proxies.

arguments.suggested_fix: Restore the check or properly handle IPv6 addresses without brackets by checking `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` (or handling bracketed vs unbracketed IPv6 addresses correctly).
arguments.explanation: In src/werkzeug/middleware/proxy_fix.py, line 164 was changed from `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` to `if ":" in x_host:`. An IPv6 address without brackets containing multiple colons (e.g., `2001:db8::1`) has a colon in it, so `x_host.rsplit(":", 1)` splits off the final component (e.g., `1`) as `SERVER_PORT` and leaves `2001:db8:` as `SERVER_NAME`, which is incorrect and breaks host parsing for raw IPv6 addresses.

evidence.note: proxy_fix.py unconditionally splits x_host on the last colon if colon is present, breaking raw IPv6 addresses without brackets or ports.
The previous check verified not x_host.endswith("]") to prevent IPv6 without brackets/port from being split incorrectly.

arguments.claim: Removing the check for endswith("]") causes an IPv6 address without brackets and containing colons (e.g. raw IPv6 address like 2001:db8::1) passed in X-Forwarded-Host to be incorrectly split by rsplit(":", 1), corrupting SERVER_NAME and SERVER_PORT.

text: Accepted.

claim: Removing the check for endswith("]") causes an IPv6 address without brackets and containing colons (e.g. raw IPv6 address like 2001:db8::1) passed in X-Forwarded-Host to be incorrectly split by rsplit(":", 1), corrupting SERVER_NAME and SERVER_PORT.

finding.title: Removing the check for endswith("]") causes an IPv6 address without brackets and containing colons (e.g. raw IPv6 address like 2001:db8::1) passed in X-Forwarded-Host to be incorrectly split by rsplit(":", 1), corrupting SERVER_NAME and SERVER_PORT.
finding.explanation: In src/werkzeug/middleware/proxy_fix.py, line 164 was changed from `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` to `if ":" in x_host:`. An IPv6 address without brackets containing multiple colons (e.g., `2001:db8::1`) has a colon in it, so `x_host.rsplit(":", 1)` splits off the final component (e.g., `1`) as `SERVER_PORT` and leaves `2001:db8:` as `SERVER_NAME`, which is incorrect and breaks host parsing for raw IPv6 addresses.
finding.suggested_fix: Restore the check or properly handle IPv6 addresses without brackets by checking `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` (or handling bracketed vs unbracketed IPv6 addresses correctly).

evidence.note: proxy_fix.py unconditionally splits x_host on the last colon if colon is present, breaking raw IPv6 addresses without brackets or ports.
The previous check verified not x_host.endswith("]") to prevent IPv6 without brackets/port from being split incorrectly.

findings.title: Removing the check for endswith("]") causes an IPv6 address without brackets and containing colons (e.g. raw IPv6 address like 2001:db8::1) passed in X-Forwarded-Host to be incorrectly split by rsplit(":", 1), corrupting SERVER_NAME and SERVER_PORT.
findings.explanation: In src/werkzeug/middleware/proxy_fix.py, line 164 was changed from `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` to `if ":" in x_host:`. An IPv6 address without brackets containing multiple colons (e.g., `2001:db8::1`) has a colon in it, so `x_host.rsplit(":", 1)` splits off the final component (e.g., `1`) as `SERVER_PORT` and leaves `2001:db8:` as `SERVER_NAME`, which is incorrect and breaks host parsing for raw IPv6 addresses.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the check or properly handle IPv6 addresses without brackets by checking `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` (or handling bracketed vs unbracketed IPv6 addresses correctly).

evidence.note: proxy_fix.py unconditionally splits x_host on the last colon if colon is present, breaking raw IPv6 addresses without brackets or ports.
